raw_posts.name: Vaani Developer Platform
raw_posts.tagline: The only voice AI harness that you'll ever need
raw_posts.description: Build a voice agent that sounds and behaves human without writing a single line of code. Design the call flow, handle objections and edge cases, connect your tools and knowledge base, and go live on a real phone number. Every call ends with clean, structured data.

raw_posts.name: Knocket AI
raw_posts.tagline: Chat with visitors from your website or link
raw_posts.description: Give visitors a way to say hello. Add free live chat to your website or app, or turn your bio link into a personal contact page. Visitors can start chatting without signing up. Built for founders, creators, and small teams.

raw_posts.name: SpeakON Agent
raw_posts.tagline: Turn natural speech into real work for an agent to complete
raw_posts.description: Turn natural speech into real work with SpeakON Agent. It understands your Notes, connects your tools, and prepares Actions for you to review and confirm.

raw_posts.name: Canva Brush
raw_posts.tagline: A vision-language model that edits your designs
raw_posts.description: Canva Brush is a vision-language model for design from Canva Research. It sees your design, understands how it’s put together, and makes the changes you ask for, from one line of copy to every slide in a deck. Everything stays fully editable. Canva says it’s up to 69% faster and 46% lower cost per edit task than its previous design agent. It’s powering Canva AI design edits for Canva Pro subscribers today.

raw_posts.name: MCP Server by XWiki
raw_posts.tagline: Give your AI your wiki's knowledge while keeping the control
raw_posts.description: XWiki MCP Server is an open-source, self-hostable extension that connects XWiki to the AI agent of your choice: OpenCode, Pi, Codex, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, and more. You can already use the extension to query your knowledge base to get answers, create and edit pages, and work with structured data directly in XWiki. Try out the extension and let us what's should we improve next!

raw_posts.name: fastbrowse
raw_posts.description: A fast open-source browser agent. It reads every button, link and field on the page and has a System One model (ex: jev) pick the next step from that list. If it's unsure, it falls back to a standard model model. Fast, cheap, and every answer provides a citation.

raw_posts.name: Chopstick
raw_posts.tagline: Mac activity and action widgets that write themselves
raw_posts.description: Chopstick notices what you repeat on your Mac and builds notch widgets for it, using the coding agent you already have. Your activity log stays local.

raw_posts.name: Teable Mobile
raw_posts.tagline: Build the systems your team runs on, now from your phone
raw_posts.description: Explain your process like you would to a new hire. Teable builds the database, the app and the automations, so the work stops living in your head. Now you can do it from your phone: hold to talk, publish to your team, and get notified when it's done.

raw_posts.name: iSurge
raw_posts.tagline: Activity monitor, per-app volume, disk cleanup at your notch
raw_posts.description: iSurge is one app for people who live on their Mac: live stats at the notch, each app's volume and mic, disk clean-up, an uninstaller, dev tools for ports, projects and Homebrew, a focus timer and Keep Awake. $14.99 once, $10.99 with PHPROMO20. No account.

raw_posts.name: Faylee
raw_posts.tagline: Bug reports your coding agent can fix from one link
raw_posts.description: Faylee records the screen, console, every network request and each click behind a bug, on one timeline, and shares it all as one link. Your team opens it and sees exactly what broke, with the failing request already open. Paste the link into Claude Code, Codex or Cursor, and Faylee's MCP server gives the agent the whole report so it can find the cause and fix it. Instant replay saves the last few minutes after a bug already happened. Free for up to 3 members.
